text: The stop condition is part of the product. A review system needs a defined response to rejection. In Resume Gauntlet, blocking outcomes keep the workflow unresolved, bounded fix loops attempt repairs, and missing verification must be reported. A completion message cannot be the only evidence that the work completed. Reuse is useful when its conditions are explicit. An unchanged artifact and unchanged review requirements can justify carrying prior work. When either changes, the workflow needs to determine what must be checked again. Repeating every step wastes effort; carrying every old verdict hides risk. That is the practical question I take from this reading: where is additional parallel work likely to change the answer, and where do I instead need a stronger contract between the work and its verification? For systems I build, I want the stopping rule to be something I can inspect and test.

text: Coordinates are part of the visual design. Pointer events arrive in browser coordinates. The shader works in drawing-buffer pixels, with a different vertical origin. The implementation accounts for the renderer’s pixel ratio and flips the pointer’s vertical coordinate before sending it to the material.
